dedupe_keys.name: dtu space magnetic ground stations in greenland the faroe islands and denmark

description: DTU Space monitors the Earth's magnetic field with a network of ground stations in Greenland, the Faroe Islands and Denmark. In Greenland it operates 18 stations at coastal locations and one on the ice cap (Summit), and it formerly ran five ice cap stations with Virginia Tech. All stations give full vector geomagnetic field data at 1 Hz resolution, and four of them (IAGA codes THL, GDH, NAQ and BFE) are geomagnetic observatories calibrated to INTERMAGNET standards. The page gives magnetogram stack plots, maps and a table of stations with IAGA codes, geodetic and quasi-dipole geomagnetic coordinates, data latency (most online, some one to five months) and years of operation, with records at some sites going back to the early 1980s and at observatories to 1926 or 1956. Access to the plots and data is free, under the DTU data policies linked from the page; no licence is named on the station page. Caveats: some stations have closed, and latency varies by station. Coverage is Greenland, the Faroe Islands and Denmark. It supports hazard exposure analysis of geomagnetically induced currents in power grids and pipelines, and space weather effects on high-latitude communications; related records are the Tromsø Geophysical Observatory data and the WDC for Geomagnetism Copenhagen.
